p: The apostasy of the latter times should not surprise us, because it was expressly foretold by the Spirit. The Spirit is God, otherwise he could not certainly foresee such distant events, which as to us are uncertain and contingent, depending on the tempers, humours, and lusts of men. The difference between the predictions of the Spirit and the oracles of the heathen is remarkable; the Spirit speaks expressly, but the oracles of the heathen were always doubtful and uncertain. It is comfortable to think that in such general apostasies all are not carried away, but only some.

Every creature of God is good: when the blessed God took a survey of all his works, God saw all that was made, and, behold, it was very good, Gen. i. 31. The blessing of God makes every creature nourishing to us; man lives not by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God (Matt. iv. 4), and therefore nothing ought to be refused. We ought therefore to ask his blessing by prayer, and so to sanctify the creatures we receive by prayer.

x.h: Exhortation to Godliness; Exhortation to Ministerial Duties. (a. d. 64.)
p: The best way for ministers to grow in knowledge and faith is to put the brethren in remembrance; while we teach others, we teach ourselves. Those whom ministers teach are brethren, and are to be treated like brethren; for ministers are not lords of God's heritage.

The best way for ministers to avoid being despised is to teach and practise the things that are given them in charge. No wonder if ministers are despised who do not teach these things, or who, instead of being examples of good to believers, act directly contrary to the doctrines they preach; for ministers are to be ensamples of their flock. Those ministers that are the best accomplished for their work must yet mind their studies, that they may be improving in knowledge; and they must mind also their work; they are to give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.

The care of ministers should be in the first place to save themselves: "Save thyself in the first place, so shalt thou be instrumental to save those that hear thee." Ministers in preaching should aim at the salvation of those that hear them, next to the salvation of their own souls. The best way to answer both these ends is to take heed to ourselves, &c.
